name: Indiana
note: Indiana registers deaths electronically in the Indiana Death Registration System (IDRS). The funeral director (or the last attending physician, PA or APRN) starts the record, and the practitioner certifies the cause to the local health officer, who is the local registrar. Each of these hops has a five-day limit. A permit for disposal is issued only on a properly executed certificate. The Indiana Department of Health must send death data to the election division for voter cancellation and to FSSA, which must check it monthly to remove deceased Medicaid enrollees. Local health officers send quarterly death records to the county auditor and the county voter registration office. A non-certified, SSN-redacted copy of a death certificate is a public record. Certified copies need a direct interest, which expressly includes beneficiaries of life insurance, annuities, retirement and transfer-on-death accounts.

steps.title: Determine death under accepted medical standards
steps.who: The practitioner determining death (the Uniform Determination of Death Act does not name the profession).
steps.trigger: Irreversible cessation of circulatory and respiratory functions, or of all brain functions.
steps.summary: Indiana enacts the Uniform Determination of Death Act. It does not say which professions may pronounce.

steps.title: Report violent or suspicious deaths to the coroner or police
steps.trigger: Discovery of a body of a person who died from violence, in a suspicious, unusual or unnatural manner, or at under three years of age.
steps.summary: Knowingly failing to notify immediately is a Class B infraction, or a Class A misdemeanor if meant to hinder an investigation. The coroner then notifies law enforcement and takes custody of the body.

steps.title: Physician refers non-natural or uncertain deaths to the coroner
steps.who: The emergency department physician (after consulting the attending physician if available). Failing that, the attending physician, and failing that, the local health officer.
steps.trigger: Circumstances suggesting a non-natural death, or an emergency department death where the cause and manner are uncertain.
steps.summary: The coroner investigates. Only the coroner may then report the death on the official certificate.

steps.title: Funeral director starts the record in IDRS and sends it to the certifier
steps.who: The person in charge of interment (funeral director), or the last attending physician, PA or APRN, whoever starts the record. Personal data come from the persons best qualified to give them.

deadline.text: not later than five days after the death

steps.summary: If the funeral director starts the record, they must send the certificate electronically to the last attending practitioner within five days of death.

steps.title: Certify the cause of death electronically to the local health department
steps.who: The physician, physician assistant or APRN last in attendance. If there was no medical attendance or the practitioner cannot sign, the local health officer inquires and certifies.
steps.trigger: Starting the record, or receiving it from the funeral director.

deadline.text: not later than five days after initiating or receiving the record

steps.summary: Certification goes through IDRS to the local health officer, who is the local registrar. Reckless violations of the chapter are Class B misdemeanors. Licensed professionals face only licensing sanctions.

steps.title: Coroner files the certificate after investigation

deadline.text: within seventy-two hours after completion of the death investigation

steps.summary: The coroner files with the county health department of the county where the death occurred. A 'pending investigation' certificate may be filed first.

steps.title: Permit for disposal issued on the executed certificate
steps.who: The local health officer in the county of death, to the person in charge of interment.
steps.trigger: Receipt of a properly executed certificate of death (or a provisional certificate where rules allow).

deadline.text: before disposition or removal of the body from the county

steps.summary: Registration gates disposition. No burial, cremation or removal from the county without the permit.

steps.title: Local health officer reports the death to the Indiana Department of Health
steps.trigger: Electronic receipt of the completed certificate.

deadline.text: not later than five days after receiving the completed certificate

steps.summary: IDRS is the electronic system for all deaths in Indiana.

steps.title: Certified copies to applicants with a direct interest
steps.who: The state registrar or any local health officer (from IDRS, regardless of where it was filed). Applicants need a direct interest, and the certificate must be necessary for personal or property rights or legal compliance.
steps.summary: Beneficiaries of an IRA, retirement account, transfer-on-death brokerage account, annuity or life policy have a direct interest by statute. On request the cause of death may be left off the copy.

steps.title: Quarterly death records to the county auditor
steps.who: The local health officer, to the county auditor.
steps.trigger: Deaths in the jurisdiction in the previous three months.

deadline.text: not later than January 31, April 30, July 31 and October 31

steps.summary: The county auditor receives a quarterly death record.

steps.title: Quarterly death records and certificates to the county voter registration office
steps.who: The local health officer, to the county voter registration office.
steps.trigger: Deaths in the jurisdiction in the previous three months.
steps.summary: A copy of each death certificate accompanies the quarterly records. The county office must cancel the registration of each voter identified as deceased.

steps.title: Indiana Department of Health reports deaths to the election division
steps.who: The Indiana Department of Health, to the election division. Local health officers report deaths and burial permits to the department.
steps.trigger: Registered deaths, including deaths of Indiana residents in other counties or other states.

deadline.text: at least once each month for out-of-state deaths

steps.summary: The department and the statewide voter list are coordinated so county offices can cancel deceased voters on an expedited basis. Deceased voters' Social Security numbers may be disclosed for this purpose.

steps.title: Deaths of Indiana residents in other states via STEVE and EVVE
steps.who: Other states' vital records offices, directly or through NAPHSIS's STEVE and EVVE systems.
steps.trigger: Death of an Indiana resident outside Indiana.

deadline.text: forwarded at least once each month

steps.summary: The Indiana Department of Health must acquire this data and forward it for voter list maintenance.

steps.title: Vital statistics to FSSA to remove deceased Medicaid enrollees
steps.who: The Indiana Department of Health, to the office of the secretary of family and social services (Medicaid).
steps.summary: FSSA must review the department's vital statistics at least monthly to remove deceased individuals from Medicaid.

steps.title: Obituaries and funeral-home notices trigger voter cancellation
steps.who: A newspaper that may carry legal notices, or a licensed funeral director's website. The family may also send a death certificate.
steps.trigger: Publication of an obituary, notice of estate administration or other death notice.
steps.summary: The county voter registration office must cancel a registration on a copy of the death certificate or a qualifying published notice. It may ask for more information if identification is insufficient.

steps.title: Anyone may inspect and copy a non-certified death certificate
steps.who: Any requester, including banks, insurers and data firms, from a local health department or the state department.
steps.summary: A death certificate is a public record for inspection and non-certified copying, with the SSN redacted. Local health officers' permanent death indexes (name, sex, age, place of death, residence) are also open to inspection. There is no verification service or data feed.

steps.title: Beneficiaries present certified copies to insurers and account custodians
steps.who: The family or a named beneficiary.
steps.trigger: A claim on a life policy, annuity, retirement or transfer-on-death account.
steps.summary: Statute gives these beneficiaries a direct interest to obtain certified copies themselves. No statutory duty on insurers or banks to check deaths was found.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Indiana sets no single filing deadline from death. The funeral director must send the record to the certifier within 5 days of death, the certifier certifies within 5 days of receipt, and the local health officer reports to the state within 5 days of that. A disposal permit requires the executed certificate.

informantDuty.note: Either the last attending physician, PA or APRN or the person in charge of interment (funeral director) may start and file the record. The certifier must complete the medical part.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: County coroners get referred cases only. There is no independent review of ordinary certificates.

electronicRegistration.note: IDRS is mandatory for funeral directors, physicians, PAs, APRNs, coroners and local health departments. Paper is allowed only during a declared outage of more than 48 hours.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register. IDRS is an event register.

governmentPropagation.note: By statute registered deaths go to the election division, county voter offices, county auditors and FSSA (Medicaid) without any request from the family. No statutory feed to the BMV or the Department of Revenue was found. Federal feeds are in the us-federal layer.

certificateAccess.note: A non-certified copy with the SSN redacted is a public record. Certified copies need a direct interest and a need for personal or property rights. Financial-account and insurance beneficiaries qualify by statute.

privateSectorVerification.note: Private bodies can inspect or copy non-certified death certificates and the local permanent death indexes. There is no official verification service or data feed.

gaps: No Indiana statute was found that requires the Department of Health to notify the Bureau of Motor Vehicles to cancel a driver licence. IC 3-7-45-2.2 assumes the BMV reports deaths to the election division but its source was not traced. Title 9 catchlines were scanned for 'death' and 'deceased'.

No statute was found that requires notice to the Department of State Revenue. The county auditor receives quarterly death records (IC 16-37-3-9(d)), apparently for property-tax deductions, but the auditor's use of them was not traced.
Which professions may pronounce death (e.g. registered nurses) was not established. IC 1-1-4-3 is profession-neutral.
The state department's rules under IC 16-37-1-3 (410 IAC) on provisional certificates and record content were not read.
Whether Indiana's EDRS transmits deaths to SSA is not in the Code read here. That is left to the us-federal layer.
